outages.place: Southern Odisha, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Kandhamal, and Boudh
outages.affected: TPSODL, as reported by OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray on Nov 20, 2026, said it had restored electricity supply to 1,069,026 consumers (written as 10,69,026 in those reports) after Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur on Friday morning, achieving 98.68 percent restoration — nearly 99 percent — across its eight-district operational area within seven hours. Those reports said all six affected 33 kV feeders, all 19 affected 33/11 kV power substations, and all 42 affected power transformers were restored, and that 364 of 365 affected 11 kV feeders and 35,749 affected distribution transformers had been restored. District-wise restoration was reported as 99.76 percent in Ganjam, 99.53 percent in Koraput, 98.90 percent in Gajapati, 98.06 percent in Rayagada, 98.01 percent in Nabarangpur, 97.55 percent in Boudh, 94.23 percent in Kandhamal, and 100 percent in Malkangiri. TPSODL CEO Amit Kumar Garg, quoted in those reports, said the company had achieved nearly 99 percent restoration. An earlier Nov 20 Odisha Stand report from Berhampur said TPSODL had reported that Cyclone Akvan affected 1,083,348 consumers across its operational area, including 534,361 in Ganjam district and 123,252 in Nabarangpur district. No official remaining-outage count, and no official estimated time for full restoration of remaining customers, was stated in the later OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray reports. No later official remaining-outage count from TPSODL or the Odisha government was found as of 11:55 AM CT Friday.

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20
outages.affected: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a statement reported by Ukrinform at 1:41 p.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (5:41 a.m. CT), said that during the night and morning Russia had launched another large-scale attack on critical energy infrastructure — power plants and substations of electricity transmission and distribution systems — and that nuclear power plants were forced to reduce their generation capacity. The ministry said a return to normal operating procedures would take place gradually after damaged networks were restored. As of Friday morning, the ministry said, some consumers remained without power in the city of Kyiv and in the Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Odesa, Kharkiv, Kherson, Cherkasy, and Chernihiv regions. Ukrinform's English report described that list as "Kyiv and 11 regions" while naming those same 10 regions plus Kyiv; the named list is used here. Ukrainska Pravda, in a 10:26 a.m. EET Friday report (2:26 a.m. CT) citing the Energy Ministry at 10:13 a.m. EET Friday (2:13 a.m. CT), and UNN, in an 8:21 a.m. EET Friday report (12:21 a.m. CT) also citing the Energy Ministry, published the same named list of Kyiv and those 10 regions. The Energy Ministry said that to stabilize the power system, emergency outages were being implemented in the city of Kyiv and in the Lviv, Zakarpattia, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Ivano-Frankivsk regions, and that a return to forecast hourly schedules would take place after the situation in the power system stabilized. It said two energy workers were injured in the Kharkiv region as a result of the attack and were taken to hospital. Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 6:43 p.m. EET Friday (10:43 a.m. CT) and by UNIAN at 7:18 p.m. EET Friday (11:18 a.m. CT), said that on Saturday, Nov 21, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country because of the aftermath of attacks on the power system. Ukrenergo said all categories of consumers would face hourly outage schedules of 1.5 to 3 groups, and that industry would face capacity-restriction schedules. UNIAN, citing Ukrenergo, said those 1.5 to 3 queues for household consumers should correspond to outages of 6 to 12 hours, and that the hourly schedules for the public and the industrial restrictions would both run throughout Saturday. LB.ua, also citing Ukrenergo, said that as a result of Russia's massive Nov 20 attack, emergency power cuts were introduced; that emergency outages were applied in the Lviv, Zakarpattia, and Ivano-Frankivsk regions; and that in Kyiv, parts of the Pecherskyi, Solomianskyi, Holosiivskyi, Dniprovskyi, and Darnytskyi districts were left without power. No official nationwide customer count was given. A midday Friday recheck at 11:55 AM CT Friday found no later official nationwide customer count or official confirmation that the Friday emergency outages had ended.

outages.cause: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20. DTEK said Friday morning that emergency outages were in effect in Dnipro city and in the Dnipro, Samarivka, Pavlohrad, and Kamianske districts, and that hourly schedules did not apply there. Ukraine's Energy Ministry said consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power as of Friday morning and that emergency outages were being implemented there
outages.affected: DTEK, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 10:26 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (2:26 a.m. CT), said at 8:47 a.m. EET Friday (12:47 a.m. CT) that emergency outages had been introduced in part of Dnipropetrovsk region, and that in Dnipro city and in the Dnipro, Samarivka, Pavlohrad, and Kamianske districts emergency outages were in effect and hourly schedules did not apply. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, as reported by Ukrinform at 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (5:41 a.m. CT) and by Ukrainska Pravda and UNN earlier Friday morning, said that as of Friday morning some consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power, and that emergency outages were being implemented in Dnipropetrovsk region, among other regions, to stabilize the power system. No official customer count for Dnipro or Dnipropetrovsk region was given in those Friday statements. No later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found. Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 9:31 a.m. EET Thursday, Nov 19 (1:31 a.m. CT) and by Ukrinform at 12:13 p.m. EET Thursday (4:13 a.m. CT), said that as of Thursday morning consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power after Russian attacks over the previous 24 hours, and that emergency outages were currently being implemented in Dnipropetrovsk, along with the Sumy, Poltava, and Kharkiv regions, because of damage to energy equipment. Censor.NET, in a 12:50 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:50 a.m. CT) citing First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov, likewise listed Dnipropetrovsk among the five regions with consumers left without electricity and among the regions under emergency outages. RBC Ukraine, in an 11:04 a.m. EET Thursday report (3:04 a.m. CT) also citing Nekrasov, likewise listed Dnipropetrovsk among the regions remaining without power as of the morning, but did not include it in the emergency-outage list in that report. No official customer count for the region was given in those Thursday-morning reports. That Thursday-morning official status is later than Wednesday reports that emergency outages were not being applied in the region. D1, in a noon EET Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing energy companies, had said that as of Wednesday morning emergency outages were not being applied in Dnipropetrovsk region and that stabilization (scheduled hourly) outages were in effect throughout the day by Ukrenergo order; Dnepr.info likewise said emergency outages had been cancelled on Wednesday. Dnipro.tv, in a 9:55 p.m. EET Wednesday report (1:55 p.m. CT) citing DTEK, said stabilization-outage schedules would be in effect in Dnipropetrovsk region on Thursday, Nov 19, for all six consumer groups throughout the day; that Thursday schedule is not a new official customer count. The latest official customer count found remains DTEK's Tuesday-morning figure. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17 report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power in Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named those districts. No official restoration time was given. This is a later, separate wave of outages from Monday evening, Nov 16, when DTEK, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 6:59 p.m. EET, said that after an attack on energy facilities in the region, the city of Dnipro was completely without power, and that some residents of the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, and Kamianskyi districts were also without electricity. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov, in a Monday Telegram post reported by NV at 7:10 p.m. EET, said that after Russian attacks on the city, almost half of Dnipro was without electricity, and he called it the sixth blackout in two weeks. Zelenskyy, in the evening address reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), said the situation was also difficult in Dnipropetrovsk region; he did not give a customer count for the region. No later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found. A midday Thursday recheck at 12:05 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure. An evening Thursday recheck at 5:50 PM CT Thursday likewise found no later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure. outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20
outages.affected: 41,000 households without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 11:27 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (3:27 a.m. CT), and by Ekonomichna Pravda at 10:55 a.m. EET Friday (2:55 a.m. CT). Both reports said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 20 hit a DTEK energy facility, and that power engineers would begin inspecting surviving equipment, carrying out repairs, and resuming the electricity supply as soon as the security situation permits. The company did not announce a timeframe for the work. Odesa regional military administration head Oleh Kiper, in a Friday Telegram post reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 10:26 a.m. EET Friday (2:26 a.m. CT), said that in the morning Russian forces had attacked a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility, that according to preliminary data there were no casualties, and that as a result of the attack more than 41,000 consumers in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts were temporarily without power. He said energy workers were assessing the consequences and working to restore supply. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 statement, said that during an air-raid alert there had been power outages in Odesa district, including in the city of Odesa, that specialists would inspect equipment and begin repairs as soon as the security situation allowed, and that the first priority was to restore supply to critical infrastructure, followed by gradual reconnection of household customers. That official statement did not give a customer count. Interfax-Ukraine, in a 12:02 p.m. EET Friday report (4:02 a.m. CT) citing DTEK's Telegram channel, likewise said outages had occurred in Odesa and Odesa district during the morning attack, and that Ukrenergo had reported a large-scale power outage in Odesa and surrounding districts. Interfax-Ukraine, citing the official Odesa city Telegram channel, said movement of all trams and trolleybuses had been temporarily suspended because of the power cut. No later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 20 outage was found. A midday Friday recheck at 11:55 AM CT Friday, including DTEK OEM's official Nov 20 statement that outages were recorded in Odesa district, including Odesa, during an air-raid alert, found no later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 20 41,000-household outage.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. DTEK said engineers would begin inspections, repairs, and restoration as soon as the security situation permits, and did not announce a timeframe.

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Torez, Debaltseve, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy said a large regional outage beginning at 3:30 p.m. on Nov 19 had been restored by 3:20 a.m. on Nov 20, but that the situation remained difficult, with new morning outages and forced temporary cuts because of a capacity deficit. On Friday, the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as reported by MK Donbass, said a capacity deficit was being caused by damage to transmission networks and substations from UAV attacks, and that temporary outages were being used to avoid further accidents.
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, in a Nov 20 morning statement posted by DNR News at 12:36 (3:36 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), said that at 3:30 p.m. on Nov 19 an emergency in the regional power system had caused large-scale electricity outages, and that after repair and commissioning work, electricity supply to all consumers disconnected by that accident had been restored by 3:20 a.m. on Nov 20, including in Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Dokuchaievsk, and the Novoazovsk, Volodarske, and Volnovakha municipal districts. It said the situation in the power system remained difficult, that new supply disruptions were recorded on Friday morning for various reasons, and that new emergencies had been recorded in the Volnovakha, Volodarske, and Shakhtarsk municipal districts and in Yenakiieve and Khartsyzk. It said forced temporary outages because of a shortage of available capacity, and to prevent equipment overloads and new large-scale accidents, were partially affecting Donetsk, Makiivka, Torez, Snizhne, and the Shakhtarsk and Amvrosiivka municipal districts, and that repair work accompanied by temporary outages was under way in Ilovaisk and some settlements in Horlivka. MK, in a Friday, Nov 20 report timed at 12:33 (3:33 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), cited Donetsk occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin as saying that more than 20,000 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk. MK quoted Kulemzin as saying that in Donetsk's Proletarskyi district, 72 transformer substations had been de-energized and 19,544 subscribers remained without electricity, and that in the Leninskyi district, 31 transformer substations had been partially de-energized because the network load had exceeded the allowable limit, leaving 3,550 subscribers without power. Kulemzin said work to restore electricity supply was under way. Those Friday morning city figures were not presented as a region-wide total covering Makiivka, Mariupol, and other cities. A later Kulemzin statement, posted by DNR News, said that according to Donetskenergo, six transformer substations in the Leninskyi district had automatically tripped, leaving 872 subscribers without electricity, and that restoration work was under way. That later statement did not give a remaining figure for the Proletarskyi district or a later citywide total. No independently confirmed customer count, and no later official region-wide remaining total, was found as of 11:55 AM CT Friday.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as reported by RIA Novosti at 1:16 p.m. Moscow time Thursday, Nov 19 (4:16 a.m. CT), said supply would be restored to consumers in stages as damage was repaired, the system stabilized, and technical possibility appeared. The later Thursday-afternoon ministry update, reported by RIA Novosti at 5:52 p.m. Moscow time Thursday (8:52 a.m. CT), did not give a firm restoration time. That is not an official firm restoration time.

outages.cause: Occupation utility Krymenergo said Friday, Nov 20, that additional electricity-consumption restrictions had been introduced and that Alushta and Sudak had been completely de-energized for urgent network repairs. Occupation authorities, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, have said a power deficit on the peninsula began after Oct 24 attacks on transmission networks outside the peninsula, which those sources attributed to Ukrainian drones; that attribution was not independently confirmed
outages.affected: No official customer count was given. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a report published at 12:40 p.m. and updated at 12:45 p.m. Friday, Nov 20 (3:40 a.m. and 3:45 a.m. CT if the times are Moscow time), citing Krymenergo, said that on Friday afternoon additional restrictions on electricity-consumption regimes had been introduced, and that residents of 12 districts, five urban districts, and two cities would be without power for three to six hours. It listed the de-energized districts as Bakhchysarai, Bilohirsk, Kirovske, Dzhankoi, Krasnohvardiiske, Lenine, Pervomaiske, Nyzhnohirskyi, Rozdolne, Saky, Simferopol, and Sovietskyi, and said there was also no power in the urban districts of Simferopol, Yevpatoria, Kerch, Feodosia, and Yalta and in the cities of Saki and Dzhankoi. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a 1:38 p.m. Friday report (4:38 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time) also citing Krymenergo, said Alushta and Sudak had been completely left without electricity on Friday because of urgent repair work on the networks, quoting Krymenergo as saying electricity supply had been disconnected in the Alushta and Sudak urban districts in connection with urgent repair work. The same report said a consumption-restriction regime had been introduced in Crimea on Friday, with outages of three to six hours in populated places, and that electricity had initially been out in seven districts of the peninsula and in Yevpatoria, and also for residents of 34 streets in Simferopol. Occupation sources, as summarized in those RIA Novosti Crimea reports, have said interruptions in Crimea and Sevastopol began on Oct 24, when they said drones attacked transmission networks outside the peninsula, and that a further attack on energy facilities affecting the peninsula was made on the night of Nov 4; those accounts and attributions come from occupation sources and were not independently confirmed. No official customer count or firm restoration time was given. A midday Friday recheck at 11:55 AM CT Friday found no later official customer count and no later official restoration notice after those Friday afternoon Krymenergo statements; the 12:40 p.m. and 1:38 p.m. Friday RIA Novosti Crimea reports remained the latest official occupation-utility statements found.

Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, said Friday's additional restrictions would leave residents without power for three to six hours. No duration was given for the complete outage in Alushta and Sudak beyond the statement that it was for urgent network repairs.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Friday bulletin said that unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance
outages.affected: UNE's Friday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Friday, Nov 20, and also reported by Directorio Cubano and by Limonada 24/7 citing Cubadebate, is the latest official national forecast found: if forecast conditions hold, 1,835 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,045 MW available versus 2,850 MW of demand (a 1,805 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Friday (5:00 a.m. CT), the grid had 1,000 MW available versus 2,250 MW of demand, leaving 1,242 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,350 MW affected at midday. On Thursday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning Friday; the maximum Thursday affectation was 1,789 MW at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Thursday (5:50 p.m. CT Thursday). Thursday solar photovoltaic output was 4,320 MWh, with a maximum of 672 MW. The Friday bulletin said unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance. It said thermal generation limitations were 368 MW, and that unit 8 of Mariel was expected to enter at the evening peak with 45 MW. Official UNE sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. No official Friday evening-peak actual from UNE was found, and the Friday evening peak had not yet occurred at the time of this update. CiberCuba, in a Nov 20 daily compilation citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, reported Friday morning generation-deficit outages and some restorations on individual Havana circuits, including outages in areas such as Miramar, Sevillano, Víbora, La Lisa, San Miguel del Padrón, and Guanabo; those circuit reports are not an official Havana-wide megawatt or circuit total.

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. It said the strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water, and food production. AFP, in a Nov 17 report on the same OHCHR findings, likewise said the intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a worrying trend, and quoted the report as saying that between Oct 20 and Nov 4 some 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. That official humanitarian account is later than an Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature, which said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. Al Jazeera said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found. A Thursday-morning recheck found no later official national customer count or restoration timetable.
